items.title: Dig
items.summary:
A web utility that executes the dig command to query domain records. Can you break out of the command syntax and hijack the shell?
TL;DR Dig is a web security challenge that explores OS Command Injection. The application takes a domain name from a POST parameter and executes system("dig '" . $_POST['name'] . "';") . Because the parameter is placed inside single quotes without proper escaping, an attacker can supply a closing single quote followed by arbitrary shell commands ( '; bash -c "..."; # ) to execute arbitrary commands and retrieve the flag. items.title: Uploader
items.summary:
A file upload portal that hosts submitted assets in a public directory. Can you leverage this service to gain arbitrary code execution?
TL;DR Uploader is a web exploitation challenge highlighting an Unrestricted File Upload vulnerability resulting in Remote Code Execution (RCE). The application calculates a SHA-1 hash of the uploaded file’s content for the filename, but preserves the original user-supplied file extension and stores the file in an executable public directory ( /upload/ ). Uploading a simple PHP webshell ( <?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?> ) enables command execution and reveals the root flag.
